phases.objective: Establish one fail-closed environment branch authority contract in SQL with repository-policy fallback, preserve main as staging/source-of-change, and enforce that authority before the existing hardened Hostinger deploy executor is reached.

e2e_journeys.entrypoint: Hostinger production deploy request through the public executor module
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: The authority layer resolves omitted branch input to Production, rejects main or any other caller-selected production branch before legacy deployment logic, requires an exact commit SHA, then delegates only normalized Production authority into the existing hardened SSH executor while registry/tool policies advertise Production only and routine SSH writes remain blocked.
steps: Load environment branch authority from active platform_runtime_config when present.
Fall back to deployment-branch-policy.json only when no SQL authority row is available.
Fail closed when an existing SQL authority is disabled, malformed, or internally inconsistent.
Resolve an omitted production branch to Production and reject main or any other mismatched caller-selected branch before legacy executor dispatch.
Require and normalize an exact 40-character production commit SHA before delegation.
Delegate Production plus the normalized exact SHA to the unchanged hardened Hostinger SSH executor.
Verify migration contracts expose Production only and retain the production SSH target as non-routine/break-glass-only.
assertions: Production is distinct from main and is the production deployment authority.
SQL authority takes precedence over the repository fallback.
Invalid SQL authority never silently falls back to repository configuration.
Production branch mismatch produces a structured fail-closed error before legacy executor logic.
The public executor replaces caller branch input with the resolved Production authority before delegation.
The existing feature flag, target policy, capability envelope, credential boundary, bounded SSH transport, exact detached checkout, and readback controls remain present behind the authority wrapper.
Command, admin-tool, and execution-policy contracts do not advertise main as a production deployment branch.
Routine SSH production writes remain disabled and no provider call, credential read, external write, force push, or secret access is introduced by the migration itself.

phases.objective: Add same-cycle proof that the exact requested commit is reachable from protected Production, update generated/public request contracts to remove the legacy main option, and retire the internal compatibility allowlist after parity evidence.
